Title: PBS to reinforce unity and integrity while remaining in GRS, says president
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam wants the party to be strengthened as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven entity that remains relevant, while reaffirming its commitment to continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS).
He said the direction of the new PBS leadership would be based on three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today, ‘Unity, Stability, Integrity’.
“We may have different views and approaches, but our goal remains the same: to strengthen PBS and fight for Sabah’s future,” he said when delivering his presidential policy speech at the congress here.
He said the struggle concerning the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) was not yet over and PBS would continue to play an active role in defending Sabah’s rights and interests.
“This means our struggle is still a long one. PBS will continue to be an active, relevant and consistent voice in defending Sabah’s rights and interests. We do not want MA63 to merely become a political slogan; we want tangible implementation and results that the people can feel,” he said.
On unity, Dr Joachim said PBS needed to continue serving as a political home that united Sabahans regardless of race, religion, district or background.
He said the party would strengthen public participation by increasing the participation of Malays and Muslim Bumiputera, regaining the confidence of the Chinese community and providing greater opportunities for professionals, women and the younger generation.
“PBS does not belong to one race. PBS belongs to everyone who believes in the struggle for Sabah,” he said.
On GRS, he said PBS would continue to be a loyal, constructive and principled partner in the coalition.
Dr Joachim said PBS’ loyalty to the coalition did not mean that the party would lose its identity, but would continue to voice Sabah’s interests, including MA63, rural development, education, the economy, employment opportunities and the people’s well-being.
“We are with GRS, but we remain PBS. In terms of integrity, positions in PBS are not a gift but a trust that requires leaders to work, go to the ground, listen to the people’s problems and seek solutions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kuala Pilah Form Two student death: Cause still undetermined after post-mortem, police question 21
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A post-mortem has failed to establish the cause of death of a 14-year-old boy whose death is being investigated following allegations of bullying at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police awaiting the results of further tests.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the examination was carried out at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Jaafar Hospital in Seremban from 10.30am today,
Harian
Metro
reported.
“The post-mortem, conducted by HTJ forensic pathologist Dr Akma Nurain Fairuz Mahamad Arif, was completed at 3pm today.
“The results of the post-mortem showed that the cause of death could not be determined at this time, and we are still awaiting the results of further tests,” Alzafny was quoted as saying.
He said police had so far recorded statements from 21 people, including students, teachers and the boy’s parents, as part of the investigation.
The student was found unconscious at the school hostel last night and was taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
Police subsequently detained a 16-year-old student to assist in the investigation and opened an investigation paper under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The teenager was today remanded for six days, until October 1, to assist police with the investigation.
The Education Ministry has also ordered an immediate audit of the school following the boy’s death and said it would cooperate fully with police.

Title: Govt to announce firm measures to ensure fair wages in Budget 2027, says Anwar
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — The government will announce more decisive measures to ensure graduates secure jobs that match their qualifications and receive fair wages in Budget 2027, which will be tabled on October 9.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was currently at the final stage of preparing the budget and would formulate more concerted efforts to ensure that wage increases were commensurate with graduates’ qualifications.
“I have previously conducted a study on increases in productivity and wages. Take South Korea, for example, particularly where productivity is high, and wages have also increased accordingly.
“In Malaysia, productivity continues to increase, but wages have increased only slightly. So, we have to use the government’s authority to apply some pressure,” he said.
He said this when asked about the government’s measures to address the issue of fair wages commensurate with graduates’ qualifications during a question-and-answer session at the UiTM Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC) here today.
Asked about management issues and weaknesses at UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar said the matter needed to be studied before taking any action.
He said reports related to the matter would also be given attention through cooperation between the UiTM vice-chancellor, the Ministry of Higher Education and the Prime Minister’s Department.
“Please look into UiTM Holdings and find ways to work together with the vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister’s Department. My office will provide the necessary cooperation and input.
“Let’s not pass judgment now. Study the weaknesses first and rectify them, or change the people involved. We have changed dozens of agencies. But if there is indeed any wrongdoing, action must be taken,” he said.
Anwar said good governance was particularly important in Bumiputera agencies to ensure that they served as an example to society.
“I am stricter with Bumiputera agencies. That is right, because they should set an example,” he said.
In 2023, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigated allegations of misappropriation that resulted in losses of RM157 million incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The MACC investigation focused on several issues, particularly involving funds and several investments made by UiTM Holdings that resulted in losses amounting to millions of ringgit. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says he has not received Loke’s resignation letter
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to receive Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation letter.
“Wait for the resignation letter,” he said briefly when asked about Loke’s intention to resign from the Cabinet.
He spoke to reporters after attending the Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today.
Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on September 19 in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The Seremban MP said he would submit his resignation letter upon returning to Malaysia from China.
On the Registrar of Societies (RoS) order suspending all Perikatan Nasional (PN) activities in connection with the upcoming Melaka state election, Anwar said the matter should be referred to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
RoS issued the suspension order, effective September 23, covering all PN activities.
According to RoS, the action was taken under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 following a notice issued to PN on September 22. — Bernama

Title: ‘Not a zero-sum game’: Anwar says he wants to help Malays, but not by denying others’ rights
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he wants to help Malays in the country, while stressing that this should not come at the expense of the rights of others because it is not a “zero-sum game”.
“But I’m confident the Bumiputera agenda can be expanded with a guarantee of social justice and without breaching the guarantee of safety and comfort of the non-Bumiputera.
“I always say, it’s not a zero-sum game. I want to help the Malays because they are my people. I’m proud of their culture, their heritage,” he said in a speech at Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here, drawing loud cheers from alumni and students.
“But I ‘
tidak senang
’ (dislike) any views that insult others, that belittle others’ roles or deny the rights of others. That is my stand,” he added.
Just before making the remarks, Anwar invited UiTM alumni to select seven to 10 representatives to evaluate programmes under Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM itself, and propose improvements.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar indicated that greater attention would be given to the socio-economic development of the Bumiputera community in next month’s federal Budget compared with previous Budgets.
He said this was not intended as divisive politics, but formed part of a national agenda, as the interests of the Bumiputera majority and indigenous communities in Sabah and Sarawak could not be sidelined.
Anwar also said he would be stricter in ensuring that every ringgit allocated to Malay and Bumiputera agencies was not misappropriated or subject to “
sakau
” (theft) by anyone, another remark that drew loud cheers from the audience.

Title: Khaled Nordin: Malaysia to reinforce defence, especially in Sabah, amid South China Sea tensions
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Malaysia needs to strengthen its national defence, particularly in Sabah, as a precaution in the event of a clash between major powers in the South China Sea.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia’s main concern was the possibility of a conflict or unexpected incident in the area that could have spillover effects on the country, particularly Sabah.
“If unexpected things happen, we know the challenges in the South China Sea and the rivalry between major powers. If something happens in that geographically small area, it could also affect our country,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled said this to reporters after the launch of the National Defence Literacy programme at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
He was commenting on concerns among Sabahans following defence cooperation between the Philippines and the United States (US), which has led to increased development of military bases, including on Balabac Island in Palawan, located about 50 kilometres from Banggi Island, Kudat, Sabah.
Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia respected the Philippines’ right to strengthen its defence capabilities through cooperation with the US, but the development needed to be given attention due to Sabah’s proximity to the country.
He said Malaysia did not dispute the Philippines’ move, but as a neighbouring country, any increase in the development of military bases or the presence of military assets in the area needed to be taken into account from the national security perspective.
“Every country has its own right to strengthen its national defence.
“That is their right, and we do not dispute it, but as a neighbouring country, we are paying attention and should take measures that can help our country in terms of defence,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Woman loses RM1.15m after falling for love scam syndicate in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 26 — A farmer and agricultural product trader lost more than RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual known as Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer.
“The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.
“After the victim made payments linked to the investment, the suspect introduced a platform called ‘Veniec Lottery,’ claimed to be an effort to recover the invested money,” he said in a statement today.
He said the victim was then persuaded to make several deposits to obtain profits and bonuses, before transferring funds to seven bank accounts totalling RM1,150,034.70, from her savings as well as loans from family members.
“However, the victim was unable to withdraw the money. Then she realised that she had been scammed,” he said. The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar advised the public not to be easily deceived by individuals who use friendship or special relationships to persuade them into making investments or handing over money.
“In addition, the public is advised to check account numbers and phone numbers through the Semak Mule platform before carrying out any financial transactions.
“Those who suspect they have become scam victims are urged to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or lodge a police report,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says company losses are not a crime — fraud, abuse and ‘sakau’ are another matter
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Companies should not be penalised simply because they make losses, but action should be taken where there is fraud, abuse of power or “
sakau
”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Speaking after addressing issues including the scrutiny of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Anwar said companies could go through periods of losses as well as profits, and that losses alone should not be grounds for punishment.
“We don’t ‘
hukum
’ (punish) people because a company makes losses. We ‘
hukum
’ because there is fraud, there is abuse of power, there is ‘
sakau
’ (stealing), not because of losses,” he said during a question-and-answer session with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni and students at UiTM’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here.
Turning to UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar cautioned against passing judgment before its position had been properly examined.
“Now study UiTM Holdings, don’t ‘
hukum
’ (pass judgment) now,” he said, adding that any weaknesses should first be identified and improved, but action should be taken if abuses were found.
Earlier, a member of the audience asked Anwar whether he could direct the Higher Education Ministry or UiTM alumni to produce a report on UiTM Holdings, which the questioner claimed had accumulated more than RM100 million in unresolved losses.
Anwar indicated that the Higher Education Ministry would be involved, adding that the Prime Minister’s Department would cooperate. He also thanked UiTM’s vice-chancellor for giving full cooperation over the UiTM Holdings issue.
During the dialogue, Anwar also addressed the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, saying it had been completed before he became prime minister in 2022 amid questions over why it was only released this year.
He said the report’s release had been delayed after TH’s leadership asked for more time, amid concerns that depositors could withdraw their savings if it was made public earlier.
Anwar rejected suggestions that the report had been released as an act of “revenge”, saying decisions over investigations, prosecutions and judgments rested with the relevant authorities.
“I don’t know who is being investigated, whether they will be charged or whether action will be taken. The investigation is handled by investigating bodies — the police, the Inland Revenue Board, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission; deciding whether to charge is under the attorney general, and judges make the decisions.
“But to say we are acting out of ‘
dendam
’ (revenge), that’s not true,” he said.
Anwar also said issues involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), which is currently under scrutiny, predated his tenure as prime minister.
He said he was particularly strict about governance at Bumiputera agencies, which he said should set an example not only for Muslims but for society as a whole.

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across much of Malaysia until this evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across the country, except Sarawak, until 5pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect the whole of Perlis and Penang.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they comprise Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
The warning also covers Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Krai in Kelantan, as well as Besut, Hulu Terengganu and Dungun in Terengganu.
In Pahang, the areas involved are Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor and Klang.
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau and Kuala Pilah, while in Johor, they are Tangkak, Muar, Batu Pahat and Mersing.
In Sabah, the warning covers Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Paitan and Sandakan), Tawau (Lahad Datu and Kunak), the West Coast, Interior (Membakut, Tambunan, Keningau, Sipitang, Beaufort and Tenom) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Mindef launches national defence literacy drive to prepare public for new security threats
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) today launched the National Defence Literacy Programme to boost the public’s awareness, knowledge and understanding of national defence, security and sovereignty.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a shifting security threat landscape demands a deeper understanding of national defence, and a recognition of the role Malaysians can play in safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty.
“This is where what we call defence literacy comes in. It is an awareness, a body of knowledge and a skill that every citizen must possess,” he told reporters after launching the National Defence Literacy Programme at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and Army chief Jen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Others in attendance were MiDAS chief executive Laksdya Datuk Yusne Mokhtar, Office of Home Affairs and Research secretary Datuk Awang Shaminan Awang Ashaari, and Sabah National Security Council director Datuk Yahya Sulaiman.
Mohamed Khaled said the public must grasp the fact that security threats today are far more complex. They are no longer confined to physical or military danger, but are alive in the digital space too.
“That is exactly why we are running this Literacy Programme. We want to build the people’s resilience. When the people are resilient, it becomes a deterrent force,” he said.
He said defence literacy efforts must be sustained, so the public not only understands defence and security issues better, but also sees the role they can play in contributing to national defence. Sabah was picked as the first state to roll out the programme, before it is expanded nationwide.
Earlier in his speech, Mohamed Khaled framed national defence through three key components: defence as the nation’s fence or shield, defence as the nation’s umbrella, and defence as the anchor or pillar of a sovereign nation.
He said the defence literacy agenda is about showing the public that there are many ways to strengthen the people’s resilience.
“Ways that don’t require anyone to become a soldier or take up arms,” he said, adding that a range of awareness programmes on defence issues will be rolled out actively.
“We want the public to understand one thing clearly: defence issues no longer start with an enemy at our borders or waters. Threats to sovereignty are everywhere,” he said.
The one-day programme featured two headline segments:
Bicara Ancaman Kognitif
(Talk on Cognitive Threats) and
Bicara Pahlawan Negara
(Talk on National Warriors). They zeroed in on how threats now target public thought and perception in today’s security landscape.
The
Bicara Pahlawan Negara
session brought together Major General (Rtd) Datuk Dr Radzi Abd Hamid as moderator and four special panellists: Lieutenant General (Rtd) Datuk Seri Zain Mohd Said SP, Major General Datuk Mohd Halim Khalid PGB, Warrant Officer 1 (Rtd) Freaddey Yojod and Lance Corporal (Rtd) Abdul Rahman Maidin.
The National Defence Literacy Programme is a Mindef initiative led by the Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security (MiDAS) in collaboration with Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia.
At its core, it aims to sharpen public awareness of one simple truth: every layer of society has a role in defending the nation’s security and sovereignty. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: UiTM Jalan Othman Campus renamed in honour of Arshad Ayub, architect of institution’s early growth
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Jalan Othman Campus in Petaling Jaya has been renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman Campus in recognition of the late educationist’s contributions to the development of the institution.
Anwar said the renaming was a tribute to Arshad’s legacy, having played a key role in the development of the Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM) into UiTM, while also being known for his firm emphasis on educational quality, good governance and expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He described Arshad as a highly respected Malay educationist who was firm and uncompromising, particularly when it came to education, quality and opportunities for Malay students.
Anwar said Arshad had also maintained a strong commitment to governance and institutional integrity, rather than using Malay institutions or agencies for personal gain or allowing them to be undermined by misconduct.
“Today’s younger generation may not remember him, but as times change, many have emerged claiming to be champions of the Malay cause and speaking about the struggle for the Malays. However, not many have maintained the same commitment to good governance or refrained from using Malay institutions and agencies to enrich themselves or undermine them,” he said.
Anwar said Arshad’s legacy should therefore be viewed not only in terms of his role in establishing and strengthening the institution, but also in the way he managed it and upheld good governance, which he said contributed to the growth of ITM’s Jalan Othman campus.
He was speaking at the UiTM Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC) here today.
Also present at the gathering were Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim, UiTM Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin and Universiti Teknologi MARA Alumni Federation of Malaysia (PAUiTM) President Saiful Azhar Shaharun.
The late Arshad, who died in 2022, was the first director of ITM, serving from 1967 to 1975 before it became known as UiTM. He was regarded as a driving force behind the development of education at ITM and had also served as a ministry secretary-general.
As an immediate measure, Anwar also approved RM2.5 million to upgrade the campus.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue to prioritise the Bumiputera development agenda, including strengthening Bumiputera educational institutions and agencies, in line with the principle of social justice.
At the same time, he stressed that efforts to strengthen the Bumiputera agenda should not come at the expense of the rights and interests of the non-Bumiputera community.
“There are people who ask about the Madani Government’s attitude and position on the Bumiputera agenda. We hear it in the political discourse, sometimes through insinuations and suggestions that we are sidelining it.
“I want to give you the figures. For example, the operating and development allocation for UiTM alone, which was less than RM2 billion before the Madani Government, has increased every year. The allocation for UiTM in 2026 is RM3.08 billion.
“And now, as we approach the final weeks before the national Budget is announced on Oct 9, I want to give an assurance that our commitment to the Bumiputera development agenda and Bumiputera agencies will continue to receive attention.
“I want to demonstrate that under the Madani Government, the attention given to the development and economic, social and educational advancement of the Bumiputera is far greater than under any previous administration,” he said.
Anwar also urged UiTM alumni to play a greater role in helping the government assess and strengthen major programmes of Bumiputera agencies, particularly UiTM.
He proposed that PAUiTM select between seven and 10 alumni to evaluate the programmes, including providing views on new fields of study that should be expanded, such as artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing and healthcare.
“I will provide every opportunity and avenue for you to evaluate each major programme of Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM, so that they can be improved and enhanced,” he said.
The prime minister also stressed the importance of student welfare, particularly for those from low-income families, including ensuring that no student faces food insecurity while pursuing their studies.
As a gesture of support and appreciation for PAUiTM’s efforts, the Prime Minister approved RM100,000 each for two programmes — the TUNaS Belia NEET Programme and the UiTM Alumni Fellowship Gathering. — Bernama

Title: Akmal Nasrullah: Removing 30pc Bumiputera equity rule for private education will not weaken empowerment agenda
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Sept 26 — The removal of the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for private education institutions (IPS) will not undermine the government’s agenda to empower the community, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said implementation and follow-up measures arising from the removal of the requirement would be handled by the relevant ministries according to their respective jurisdictions.
Akmal Nasrullah said the Bumiputera empowerment agenda should instead be viewed in terms of strengthening the community’s capacity to participate in and expand its presence in the economy.
“The government will continue to strengthen the Bumiputera empowerment agenda through approaches that can increase their capacity to continue growing and participating in economic activities,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the closing ceremony of the Rehda Institute Youth Initiative (RIYI) 2026 here.
Akmal Nasrullah said the government remained focused on increasing Bumiputera participation and capabilities in economic activities, and that removing the equity requirement did not signal any reduction in its commitment to the community’s economic empowerment.
At the event, the minister was also presented with the RIYI 2026 closing summary report, which highlighted a gap between students’ expectations and employers’ assessments of graduates’ workplace readiness.
The survey found that 41.6 per cent of student respondents considered one to three months a realistic period for fresh graduates to begin adding commercial value at work, compared with just 2.9 per cent of employers who held the same view.
Meanwhile, 62 per cent of students said they felt adequately prepared by their universities, while only 32.3 per cent of employers agreed that local universities sufficiently prepared graduates for workplace realities.
The survey involved students and recent graduates from 21 Malaysian universities as well as employers, although the report cautioned that the findings came from targeted surveys and were not nationally representative.
The report also highlighted the growing impact of artificial intelligence on entry-level employment. Some 76.4 per cent of student respondents said they regularly used AI tools, while half of the employers surveyed expected AI to reduce the number of entry-level positions they would hire for over the next three years.
On career development, 79.4 per cent of employers said they were willing to provide structured training and a clear career path in return for a commitment from employees to stay, while 67.6 per cent of students said they would accept such an arrangement.
The survey also found that 82.4 per cent of students and 58.3 per cent of employers supported compulsory salary-range disclosure in job advertisements, while 57.1 per cent of students said they were likely or very likely to work outside Malaysia within five years.
The findings form part of RIYI 2026’s focus on narrowing the gap between universities and industry, with the initiative bringing students together with industry leaders to gain exposure to workplace expectations, career development and the skills needed in a technology-driven economy.
Rehda Institute chairman Datuk Jeffrey Ng Tiong Lip said closer collaboration between universities and industry was needed to give students earlier exposure to workplace realities.
“A university qualification provides an important foundation, but young people also need to understand how workplaces operate, how decisions are made and what employers expect from them.
“This is where RIYI plays an important role in bringing students closer to industry through direct engagement and mentorship, while helping them develop the judgement, resilience, communication and adaptability needed to build sustainable careers,” he said.
The RIYI 2026 programme brought together students from more than 21 universities, with its final session focusing on AI’s impact on junior roles, productivity, decision-making and the capabilities expected of future leaders.

Title: Sarawak to set up authority to manage and develop lakes, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 26 — Sarawak will establish an authority to oversee, manage and develop the state’s lake areas in a comprehensive manner.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the initiative is part of the state’s development plans for the next five years.
He said the plans took into account approaches adopted by other states to develop lake areas as resort destinations while providing better facilities.
“Insya-Allah, we will establish an authority to oversee all our lakes in Sarawak, including rivers with potential,” he said at the launch of the Sarawakku Sayang 2026 programme in Betong today.
Abang Johari said the initiative was also expected to add value to the state’s economic growth while further strengthening Sarawak’s existing strengths.
Meanwhile, he said the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak (CENTEXS) would establish a Flying School Academy in Betong to support the state’s efforts to advance modern agriculture through drone technology.
“Drones are important, in addition to aircraft, which is why I support the establishment of a flying academy here in collaboration with the private sector.
“This is because licences are required, while the open airspace here provides a conducive environment for students to learn how to operate drones in the Betong area,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kuskop channels nearly RM10b to 270,000 entrepreneurs as of August, seeks bigger Budget 2027 allocation, says minister
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 26 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) has channelled nearly RM10 billion through various support and financing programmes under the ‘Power Up 10K’ initiative to about 270,000 entrepreneurs nationwide as of the end of August.
Its minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the achievement was among the reasons Kuskop had proposed to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) for larger allocations for the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and cooperative sectors under Budget 2027.
“The RM10 billion is part of the RM15 billion target to be channelled to the MSME and cooperative sectors this year. In Penang alone, RM760 million was channelled in the first eight months, benefiting about 6,000 entrepreneurs.
“If Malaysians want to do business in Malaysia but do not have opportunities, let us not talk about overseas markets first. We must ensure Malaysian businesses, products and services can penetrate the domestic market before going abroad,” he told reporters after the 2026 “
Hebatkan Perniagaan Malaysia
” (HPM) Carnival, Penang edition, at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Sim noted that financing support for the MSME sector had been increased to RM60 billion this year from RM50 billion previously.
He said Kuskop had also proposed reducing the cost of doing business and improving government delivery efficiency to help MSMEs expand. Measures included simplifying government processes, shortening processing times and reducing related fees and charges.
“If we cannot control global oil prices, at least we can control local costs. Government processes must be made easier and processing times, fees and charges, including taxes where possible, should be reduced so that MSMEs can have some breathing space,” he said.
Sim advised that delays in obtaining licences, permits or financing could cause entrepreneurs to lose business opportunities. He added that Kuskop, through Tekun Nasional, had reduced the financing application period to seven days from 30 to 40 days previously, while financing below RM20,000 must be approved within 24 hours.
“The principles Kuskop has conveyed to MOF are, firstly, more funding for the MSME and cooperative sectors; secondly, a lower cost of doing business; and thirdly, greater government delivery efficiency,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Over 86pc of Perlis patients seen within an hour under digital medical record pilot, says Fahmi
Article:
PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The pilot Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system implemented under the National Digital Health Ecosystem and Connectivity Driver (Persada) initiative at health facilities in Perlis has had a positive impact on patient waiting times, said Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The communications minister said the project, which has been implemented in the state for the past four months, showed that more than 86 per cent of patients were able to see a doctor in less than 60 minutes, while 62.8 per cent did so in less than 30 minutes.
“It has benefited more than 200,000 patients in Perlis. I have also received some feedback on the system and made several suggestions to ensure that it is safe to use and easy for Health Ministry staff to operate,” he told reporters after inspecting the Persada project at the Padang Besar Health Clinic here today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik.
Fahmi said doctors no longer had to wait for patients’ medical records to be retrieved manually, as all relevant information could be accessed through the system.
“The doctors said the system made their work easier and reduced the time spent waiting for patients’ medical records to reach them, as they are stored in the cloud, which is more secure,” he said.
Fahmi said the ministry plans to expand the system to other states but would first assess several factors, including internet connectivity, to ensure that it could be used efficiently and effectively.
“I believe it can benefit other states, but we will look at several aspects because some states may face certain challenges. I was informed that the system requires an internet connection of at least 100 Mbps,” he said.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in a statement, said that Persada would facilitate smoother sharing of health information and lay the foundation for the implementation of the ‘One Individual, One Health Record’ aspiration.
“Patients’ health records can help ensure continuity of care when they seek treatment at different facilities or locations, providing a smoother and more organised experience while helping to reduce waiting times,” it said.
According to the statement, cross-ministerial cooperation between the Communications Ministry, through MCMC, and the Health Ministry (MOH) would help strengthen service delivery, as well as digital connectivity and the integration of technology.
Fahmi added that MCMC had integrated telehealth services through 17 National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI) in Perlis, enabling local residents to access certain services, including health screenings, at the centres without having to visit a health clinic.
“We will strengthen cooperation between NADI centres under MCMC and health clinics as well as rural clinics, not only in Perlis but nationwide, to make it easier for patients to access treatment,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nancy: Don’t just add seats — decide Sabah-Sarawak representation formula first
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 26 — Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said she and several Sarawak leaders, including in Cabinet, have raised the issue, but the focus had previously been more on state assembly seats.
“Speaking on voicing out in terms of (Parliamentary) seats, I am with Yang Berhormat Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi in Cabinet.
“How that one-third formula is to be created needs to be discussed together, in terms of legislation,” she said after the Motivation and Guidance Programme for Study Opportunities and UiTM Sarawak Branch Academic Exhibition at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Bako here today.
Nancy, who is also vice-president of the Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Women’s Movement, said further discussions to determine a suitable method and measure must be held between the Sarawak premier, Sabah chief minister and the Federal Government.
Previously, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed in principle to increase the ratio of Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the regions’ position in the formation of Malaysia through the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
He said the decision was among the key matters agreed at the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: BN to hold separate talks with two groups next week over Melaka state election cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will hold separate talks with two different groups next week as it weighs possible political partnerships ahead of the Melaka state election, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
Zahid declined to identify either group, leaving open whether the meetings would involve Perikatan Nasional (PN), Pakatan Harapan (PH) or other parties.
According to
Sinar Harian
, he said BN headquarters had arranged the meetings for different dates and times.
“Next week, the headquarters has arranged two separate meetings, on different dates and at different times. Two different groups,” he said.
“We have only just started discussions, so how can we disclose anything yet? Let us discuss it first. We will inform [Melaka BN chairman] Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.”
Asked whether BN would hold talks directly with PAS following PN’s suspension by the Registrar of Societies, Zahid said the matter should be decided by PN’s chairman and secretary-general.
“I leave that matter to the secretary-general and the PN chairman to decide, but we would be more comfortable dealing with an individual party rather than a coalition that is no longer intact,” he said.
His remarks come as PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said separately today that the coalition’s suspension had not affected its negotiations with BN, adding that the talks were more than halfway complete.
When asked which potential partner was closest to reaching an agreement with BN, Zahid said no decision had yet been made.
“That will be examined further, and we have to weigh the risks and what is reasonable, and determine which carries greater weight,” he said.
“As a political coalition under the BN banner, we naturally want to look at the medium- and long-term benefits for the country, and particularly for the parties in our coalition.”
Melaka’s 28-seat state assembly was dissolved on September 23, paving the way for the state’s 16th election.
Under the state constitution, polling must be held within 60 days of dissolution, meaning by November 22.
The Election Commission is due to meet on October 7 to set the nomination and polling dates.

Title: ‘Digitalisation should not create a divide’: Gobind urges inclusive tech push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The national digital transformation agenda must be implemented inclusively and cannot solely benefit those with access to technology.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the digitalisation process must also ensure that the digitally less literate, elderly, low-income groups and small entrepreneurs can enjoy the same benefits.
“We want technology to be a tool that makes people’s lives easier, rather than adding to their burden. We want digitalisation to open up opportunities, not create a divide,” he said during the Madani Kita Programme at the Damansara Damai Community Hall here today.
Gobind, who is also the Damansara Member of Parliament, said the national digitalisation agenda was not solely about technology, but about people.
He said technology was merely a tool and what was important was how it was used to improve people’s lives.
“This is what we mean by digital for the people. Digital is not just about applications. Digital is not just about artificial intelligence (AI). Digital is not just about data and new technologies.
“Digital is about how all these developments ultimately benefit the people,” he said.
He said the measure of a policy’s success relied not only on how many programmes were implemented, but also on the extent to which the people benefited and experienced changes in their daily lives.
Meanwhile, Gobind said the Madani Kita Programme was a platform organised to bring the government closer to the people through the involvement of various ministries, departments and government agencies in a single location.
He said the programme, implemented by Akademi Kenegaraan Malaysia (AKM), allowed the public to interact directly with government agencies, obtain information on services, understand government initiatives, and convey their views, suggestions and problems. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh suggests standardising routes to reduce road closures for KL running events
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Running event organisers in the capital are being told to standardise their routes with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to curb disruptions to the city with endless road closures.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said one fix worth considering is to set standard routes based on running distances, and make organisers stick to them.
“Three kilometres — this is the route. Five kilometres — this is the route. Organisers cannot just pick whichever route they fancy,” she told reporters after officiating the Mega Cleaning Programme for Hari Cuci Malaysia at the Batu Muda People’s Housing Programme (PPR) here today.
Hannah said the coordination is crucial because road users need to know in advance which routes are affected so they can plan their journeys.
“This week alone, 30 roads are closed for one run. I cannot accept this. I don’t want the public unable to plan their trips into the city. We need to organise these runs properly,” she said.
Hannah said the move is not aimed at stopping such events, but to ensure they can be held in a more orderly manner without disrupting traffic flow, given that more than a million vehicles enter Kuala Lumpur every day.
She said organisers who need different routes could consider less congested locations, while also making use of existing ones such as those used for the Car Free Day programme.
“Kuala Lumpur is a city that needs to be well organised. I don’t want people wasting hours waiting for roads to reopen,” she said. — Bernama

Title: PAS logo an option for Perikatan in Melaka election if RoS suspension remains, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) may contest the Melaka state election under the PAS logo if the coalition’s suspension by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) remains in force, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today.
According to
Harian Metro
, Takiyuddin said the choice of logo was not a major issue for the coalition, which would decide its approach according to the circumstances ahead of the election.
He said PAS had no difficulty contesting under its own logo, while Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia could also contest using its own symbol.
Takiyuddin added that parties in an electoral alliance did not necessarily have to use their respective logos, pointing to the 2018 general election, when DAP, PKR and Bersatu candidates contested under the PKR symbol.
“So, it is not necessary for those parties [within PN] to use their own logos. They can use the logo of any party that shows they are united together.
“So what is wrong if one of the parties in the coalition — PAS, for example — or the other parties also use that logo? There is nothing unlawful about it.
“This is among the options we have if PN remains suspended,” he was quoted as saying at the Bunut Payong Cakna Rakyat Carnival in Kota Bharu.
The RoS ordered PN to suspend all activities with effect from September 23 under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. The notice was issued following a complaint lodged with the department by Bersatu.
PN has also been issued a notice requiring it to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.
The Melaka state assembly was dissolved with effect from September 23, paving the way for the state election.
At the previous state election on November 20, 2021, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats to form the government, while Pakatan Harapan secured five and PN two.

Title: Fahmi: Govt to cover postal delivery costs for medicines from Oct 1 under MCMC-MOH initiative
Article:
PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), will help the Health Ministry (MoH) provide free postal delivery of medicines to patients who opt for the service from October 1.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would be implemented nationwide with an allocation of about RM5 million.
“Previously, patients had to pay for the postal delivery of medicines, but from October 1, they will no longer have to pay as the cost will be fully borne by the government through MCMC,” he told reporters after visiting the National Digital Health Ecosystem and Connectivity Driver (Persada) initiative project at the Padang Besar Health Clinic here today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik.
In June, Fahmi was reported to have said that the government would fully bear the cost of delivering medicines to about 80,000 patients a month under the Postal Medicine Delivery Programme (UMP), through a collaboration between MCMC and MoH. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan police chief: 16-year-old remanded six days over murder probe into Kuala Pilah Form Two student’s death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 16-year-old Form Four student detained in connection with the murder investigation into the death of a Form Two student at a Kuala Pilah school has been remanded for six days, until October 1.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the remand application was made at the Seremban Magistrates’ Court today.
“Police applied for the teenager to be remanded this morning and the court granted a six-day remand beginning today, until October 1,” he said to
Harian Metro
.
Police had earlier said the student was detained to assist investigations after the death was classified as murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Preliminary investigations found that the incident took place at the school hostel at about 8pm on Friday.
The victim was taken to Kuala Pilah Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Police are continuing to examine the evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding the death and any possible motive.
Alzafny had earlier urged the public not to speculate or circulate unverified information, saying this could interfere with the investigation and affect the privacy of the families involved.
The Education Ministry has ordered an immediate audit of the school and said it would cooperate fully with police.

Title: Malaysia says pandemic prevention and preparedness must be shared global responsibility, Tok Mat tells UN
Article:
NEW YORK, Sept 26 — Malaysia has stressed that pandemic prevention, preparedness and response must be treated as both a national imperative and a shared global responsibility, drawing on lessons from the Covid-19 pandemic.
“Covid-19 exposed a fundamental truth. No nation can secure its health in isolation,” said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in Malaysia’s statement at the High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response here yesterday.
Mohamad is in New York from September 23 to 27 to lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
Malaysia has translated this lesson into action, Mohamad shared at the meeting.
“Through the Malaysia National Action Plan for Health Security 2025–2030, we are strengthening health-system readiness, integrated surveillance and early warning, laboratory capacity, emergency coordination, and a prepared health workforce,” he said.
Taking public health seriously, Mohamad said Malaysia is implementing the ‘One Health’ approach to mitigate microbiological threats in food, water and the environment.
“We believe that only through a whole-of-society approach would public health be assured nationwide,” he said.
The foreign minister noted that stronger preparedness will remain incomplete without equity.
Malaysia, he said, welcomes the WHO Pandemic Agreement and “we call for a robust and equitable Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing Annex that places pathogen sharing and benefit-sharing on an equal footing, while respecting national legislation and State sovereignty.”
Mohamad said equity must also be supported by the capacity to research, develop and produce essential health products.
Through its National Vaccine Development Roadmap 2021–2030, Malaysia is strengthening these capabilities.
Looking ahead, Mohamad said Malaysia’s collective ambition must be matched by sustainable means.
“Financing should be adequate, predictable and responsive to public health risks, equity and country needs.
“International mechanisms must complement domestic investment, strengthen national capacities, and reinforce universal health coverage,” he said.
The true test of this meeting, Mohamad said, will not be the commitments we announce, but whether the next threat is detected earlier, contained faster and met with fairer access to life-saving tools.
“Let us make solidarity not an improvised response to crisis, but a standing commitment secured before the next emergency, for every nation and every generation,” he said.
The meeting was held under the theme “Fostering a Multilateral and Intergenerational Approach to Prevent, Prepare for and Respond to Pandemics and Public Health Emergencies, Through the Principles of Equity and Solidarity” at the UN Headquarters. — Bernama

Title: Road users call for urgent repairs along damaged Batu 32 stretch in Sandakan
Article:
SANDAKAN, Sept 26 — Road users are calling for urgent repairs to a badly damaged stretch of road along Batu 32 here, opposite the Road Transport Department (JPJ) checkpoint, following years of what they described as neglect.
Resident Mohd Hakimi raised concern over the condition of the road, describing it as a lifeline for the local community that had been left without comprehensive repairs despite its deteriorating state.
His concern intensified after he witnessed a vehicle stranded by the roadside after being disabled by the severely damaged road surface.
He said the incident highlighted the danger faced by motorists and other road users who depend on the route daily.
According to Mohd Hakimi, breakdowns caused by deep potholes, including blown tyres and damaged rims, had become increasingly common among residents using the road.
He said the deteriorating condition was not only a safety hazard but also placed an additional financial burden on vehicle owners, who had to bear repair and maintenance costs.
Mohd Hakimi questioned why basic infrastructure such as safe and properly maintained roads remained an unresolved issue despite the country having been independent for decades.
He also questioned the level of monitoring by the authorities, particularly as the damaged stretch is located near a JPJ enforcement facility.
He called on the local authority, Public Works Department (JKR) and road maintenance concessionaires to visit the site and see for themselves the difficulties faced by road users.
Mohd Hakimi said patchwork repairs were no longer sufficient, as such repairs often deteriorated again within a short period, particularly during the rainy season.
Instead, he called for comprehensive and quality resurfacing works to ensure the road remained durable in the long term.
He warned that apart from causing damage to vehicles, the poor road condition could also contribute to serious or fatal accidents, particularly involving motorcyclists and motorists travelling at night when visibility is reduced.
Residents are now hoping the relevant authorities and elected representatives will give serious attention to the matter and implement a permanent solution before the situation results in a serious accident or loss of life. — Daily Express

Title: Hannah Yeoh: DBKL allocates RM28.12m for PPR Batu Muda upgrading and maintenance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has allocated RM28.12 million for phased maintenance and upgrading works at the Batu Muda People’s Housing Programme (PPR) here.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the allocation to improve various facilities at the housing scheme was expected to benefit more than 10,000 residents, provided they took good care of the facilities.
“As long as Malaysians do not know how to maintain cleanliness, money will continue to be spent on cleaning operations, and we will not have enough funds for development,” she told reporters during the Mega Cleaning Programme in conjunction with Malaysia Clean-Up Day and a walkabout to inspect maintenance works at PPR Batu Muda today.
She stressed that maintaining cleanliness through the Malaysia Clean-Up initiative should become a continuous habit rather than merely a one-off programme.
The programme was also attended by Batu MP P. Prabakaran and Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud.
Meanwhile, DBKL said in a statement that upgrading works completed at PPR Batu Muda included the replacement of 21 lifts costing RM11.69 million, which was completed in October last year and is currently within the Defects Liability Period (DLP).
DBKL also completed road resurfacing works costing RM1.46 million, as well as the upgrading of a children’s playground at the housing scheme at a cost of RM278,000. — Bernama

Title: Tok Mat: Malaysia backs mechanism to document and expose Israeli violations at Jerusalem holy sites
Article:
NEW YORK, Sept 26 — Malaysia fully supports the establishment of a sustainable, institutional and operational mechanism, including a dedicated media platform, to document and expose Israel’s violations against the Holy Sites and worshippers in Jerusalem, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said Israel must be held accountable for its crimes and that its gross violations must not be ignored or normalised through repetition.
Mohamad said this in his intervention at the Joint Ministerial Meeting between the League of Arab States and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) on Jerusalem at the United Nations headquarters here yesterday.
He said Malaysia continued to hold the view that Jerusalem must remain at the very heart of the Ummah’s collective struggle and action.
As reaffirmed in the Amman Ministerial Statement of Aug 5, he said East Jerusalem was an integral part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) and the capital of the State of Palestine, consistent with the International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) Advisory Opinion of July 19, 2024.
“Importantly, the same Advisory Opinion reaffirms the illegality of Israel’s occupation of the OPT including East Jerusalem,” he said.
Mohamad stressed that Israel had no sovereignty over East Jerusalem.
“Any attempt to alter its Arab, Islamic and Christian identity or its legal and demographic character was unlawful and must be unequivocally rejected,” he stressed further.
Malaysia strongly condemned the escalating violations at Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif, including repeated incursions by extremist settlers and Israeli officials, restrictions on worshippers and persistent attempts to alter the historic and legal status quo.
“These provocations risk igniting a wider religious conflict with grave consequences for regional and international peace and security,” he said.
Malaysia, Mohamad said, reaffirmed its unwavering support for the historical Hashemite Custodianship over the Islamic and Christian Holy Sites in Jerusalem, as well as all efforts to protect the rights, resilience and presence of the Palestinian people in their city.
The foreign minister said the Holy City of Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) could not be truly protected through mere statements of concern or expressions of condemnation, but required “sustained coordination, collective resolve and decisive action.”
Mohamad said the time has come for “our collective voice to be matched by collective action.”
“We must therefore use all necessary means to fight and end the crimes committed by Israel on Palestinians. While we continue to demand decisive actions by the UN Security Council, we can and must also take our own actions, individually and as a group.
“We commend those that have suspended bilateral, trade and social relations with Israel, and welcome sanctions imposed on certain extremist Israeli Ministers, which should be extended to other Israeli leaders who incite hatred, dehumanise Palestinians and provoke violence.”
Malaysia, Mohamad said, reiterates “our call on all Member States to halt the provision of arms and financial support to Israel, so as not to become complicit in its illegal war and occupation.”
“Once again, Malaysia reiterates its unwavering commitment to defending the Holy City of Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) and the Palestinian cause.
“We reaffirm our solidarity with the Palestinian people and our steadfast support for their right to self-determination and the realisation of an independent State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.”
Mohamad is in New York from September 23 to 27 to lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). — Bernama

Title: Serian IPD posts unhealthy API 151 at 9am, 63 areas record moderate readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) in Sarawak recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 151 as of 9am today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 63 other areas nationwide logged moderate readings.
They included Sri Aman, Sarawak (98); Batu Pahat, Johor (81); Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (69); Klang, Selangor (62); and Kimanis, Sabah (56).
Only three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah, Kelantan (47); Langkawi, Kedah (46); and Besut, Terengganu (43).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and anything above 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Hari Cuci Malaysia 2026 targets 200,000 participants and 28,000kg of recyclables in a single day, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Some 200,000 people are targeted to participate in Hari Cuci Malaysia (HCM) 2026 nationwide, with 28,000 kilogrammes of recyclable items expected to be collected in a single day.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the targets were set to maintain the momentum of HCM, which has gained increasing public participation since its introduction in 2024.
“The target is not merely about breaking records, but reflects the breadth of public participation and the strength of the cleanliness movement that we are building together,” he told reporters after launching HCM 2026 at Pasar Taman Sri Gombak here today.
As of 9 am today, more than 95,000 people had registered online for the programme, excluding participating school students, involving 469 locations nationwide.
Nga said HCM set three Malaysia Book of Records achievements in 2024, including the largest simultaneous participation of 58,007 people, the collection of 4,645 tonnes of waste in a day and a continuous operation from 8 am to 8 pm.
Last year, the programme made history again with more than 100,000 people participating simultaneously, while more than 27,600 kilogrammes of used cooking oil were collected in a single day, setting a record for the largest collection of used cooking oil.
For the first time this year, the Education Ministry (MOE) is a strategic partner of HCM, involving 10,000 schools nationwide.
The ministry has also recognised HCM activities under the physical fitness, sports and co-curricular assessment (PAJSK), encouraging greater participation among young people in efforts to foster a culture of cleanliness.
Nga said the government was also strengthening the solid waste management agenda through the 9R approach: Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Refurbish, Remanufacture, Repurpose, Recycle and Recover.
He stressed that efforts to instil a culture of cleanliness should begin at school to encourage responsible use of resources.
HCM is also part of the Madani Government’s public cleaning reform agenda, including the implementation of Community Service Orders for littering offences from January this year.
“As of National Day this year, 15,678 compounds or cleaning offence notices had been issued, while 599 individuals had been ordered by the courts to carry out cleaning work, including sweeping roads, cleaning drains and toilets,” he said.
Meanwhile, nearly 1,000 shopping centres nationwide are required to provide recycling collection facilities from this year to ensure valuable resources can be recovered and reused.
Nga said maintaining cleanliness was not solely the responsibility of the authorities but required the participation of the entire community to keep Malaysia clean and prosperous. — Bernama
